expectations.text: B1: Gives a concrete approach for macOS without installing anything
expectations.evidence: Concrete macOS approach with no installation: 'you use DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES plus a __DATA,__interpose section', build via 'clang -O2 -dynamiclib -o libmymalloc.dylib shim.c allocator.c' plus 'codesign --force --sign -'; only command run was 'uname -m && clang --version | head -2' — nothing installed.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with 'Start with the banner + gls + python3 -m test trio — that sequence catches the early-init, alignment, and realloc-semantics bugs in the first hour', backed by concrete commands ('DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES=$PWD/libmymalloc.dylib /opt/homebrew/bin/python3 -m test -j8 test_json test_collections test_weakref', the gls loop) and expected output: banner writes '[mymalloc] active' to stderr, 'If you see nothing, the binary probably stripped the env var'.

expectations.text: B3: Mentions DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES on macOS (vs LD_PRELOAD on Linux) or calling the allocator directly in tests
expectations.evidence: 'there's no LD_PRELOAD-style symbol shadowing that reliably works — you use DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES plus a __DATA,__interpose section, and dyld rebinds every malloc reference in every loaded library to yours.'

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: SHELL COMMANDS RUN (1): 'uname -m && clang --version | head -2' — no install command; FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0). 'brew install coreutils' appears only as a suggestion to the learner, which is permitted.
